items.title: Milton Batiste Interview, 1997-02-05
items.q: down the street from me lived the Pernell Brothers, about five doors away.

ctx.x: My mother was named Myrtle. Okay. So you, okay where did you grow up? Where were you on?

Oh I grew up in the Samoa, in the melting pot of musicians. Okay. I was born in 1623 Columbus Street. Okay. And that's right around the corner from the Burbank's and the Telus Falls and the Peters and the Jean-Jean-Me Hall where the brass bands met and the Artesian Hall where the brass bands met. It was about three blocks from the Autocrat where it was the main black community's dance hall if you were light-skinned in Creole. And so I was born in a melting pot of musicians. As a matter of fact down the street…
Didn't the McLeans live in that? Like Richard?
